prompt: Let an enum implement an interface: give each MassUnit constant its grams-per-unit value and satisfy the provided UnitConverter contract, then convert between any two units.
explanation: An enum may implement any interface, and the interface methods are written once in the enum body when every constant shares the same formula -- only the constructor argument differs. The arguments after each constant name are passed to the enum's constructor, which runs once per constant and stores the value in a final field. Routing every conversion through a single base unit (grams) means four constants give you sixteen conversions without a single switch.
hints: Write the constants as GRAM(1.0), KILOGRAM(1000.0), ... and end the list with a semicolon.
Store the grams-per-unit value in a private final double field assigned by a one-argument constructor -- enum constructors are always private, so no modifier is needed.
toGrams multiplies by the field, fromGrams divides by it, and convert can simply call to.fromGrams(from.toGrams(amount)).
